structure: A single short Markdown ruling file, 72 lines (workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-ian-2026-11-11.md), from Ian, dated 11 November 2026, on what settles a difference between the V4 data dictionary (confluence:6497338582, "Live Animals & Germinals Data Dictionary") and the DR1 parity judgements (document:dr1-parity-notes, document:dr1-parity-backlog). It is laid out in three stretches. First, an untitled preamble of lines 1 to 14: the question as it arose while starting the identification-and-permanent-address theme from conflict c-334 (whether a tattoo is asked for on cattle and pigs), carrying two block quotes of Ian's own words, one on precedence ("v4 always wins over DR1, v4 is the source of truth") and one on what a row may rest on ("Double check none of these rows ... all data is either an MDM concern, or if our pages differ based on it, from the v4, not just the prototype"). Second, "## Decided", lines 16 to 63: six numbered points, each bold-led and each marked New, Unchanged or restated — V4 outranking every DR1 judgement; V4 as the source of truth for data against the prototype's app/data/*.js demo fixtures; the two owners of data, MDM content via trade-imports-reference-data under claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09 or V4; the prototype still deciding how a page looks and reads; c-334 settled on V4's tattoo list, with two sub-bullets (V4 against DR1 over commit b1ff013c, and V4 against itself over the expand title's count against its five entries); and V4 winning on shape as well as value, with the CPH allow-list of fourteen chapter-01 codes replacing main's inverted CPH_EXEMPT_CODES deny-list from fb0255c1. Third, "## What this changes in the backlog", lines 65 to 72: four bullets on req-2154 and req-2155 moving from question to adopted, the tattoo row's home in identification-and-permanent-address, the CPH allow-list item in deferred.md still needing a home, and "Nothing else" — the ruling adds no requirement that was not already extracted. Its scope in sources.json is "whole file", so nothing is left out. At 72 lines it is comfortably one part, as a ruling almost always is.

parts.title: Whole ruling
parts.scope: The whole file: the preamble and its two verbatim block quotes (lines 1 to 14), the six numbered points under "Decided" with point 5's two sub-bullets (lines 16 to 63), and the four bullets under "What this changes in the backlog" (lines 65 to 72). There is no other part.
covers: The preamble: the question is what settles a difference between the V4 data dictionary (confluence:6497338582, the page now titled "Live Animals & Germinals Data Dictionary") and the DR1 parity judgements (document:dr1-parity-notes, document:dr1-parity-backlog), raised while starting the identification-and-permanent-address theme by conflict c-334 on whether a tattoo is asked for on cattle and pigs
The first block quote verbatim: "v4 always wins over DR1, v4 is the source of truth"

The second block quote verbatim, on what a row may rest on: every row, existing or being created, is checked for being purely data-based from the prototype, and all data is either an MDM concern or, where our pages differ based on it, from the V4 and not just the prototype

Decided point 1: V4 outranks every DR1 judgement on every point with no exception; where V4 and a DR1 parity note or backlog row describe the same thing differently, V4 is built and the DR1 judgement is set aside; this is wider than ruling:sam-2026-10-07's "a DR1 judgement on that same difference" overriding the prototype and wider than confluence:6497338582's role already outranking the prototype on data, neither of which said what happens when V4 and DR1 disagree; a deliberate DR1 parity commit is not a reason to keep DR1's answer, it is the change V4 reverses; marked New

Decided point 2: V4 is the source of truth for data; no row may rest on the prototype's app/data/*.js files for what data a notification captures, which values a field offers, or which commodities a rule covers; those files are demo fixtures written to make the prototype's pages demonstrable; a claim of kind data taken from them is evidence of nothing except what the prototype happened to hard-code; marked New as a general rule, already applied to the commodity catalogue when inc-012 was dropped on 3 November

Decided point 3: every piece of data belongs to one of two owners and neither is the prototype — either a reference list, which is MDM's content reaching the service through trade-imports-reference-data under claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09, never a reason to block a row and never edited in code; or a field, format, limit, level or conditional rule the notification captures, which V4 specifies; a row that cannot point to one of those two owners for the data it asserts is not a row; marked New

Decided point 4: the prototype still decides how a page looks and reads — which fields a page shows and in what order, their labels, hints, error messages, captions, headings and the journey's question order; that is not data and nothing here narrows it; where V4 specifies the same field's format, limit, level or whether it is mandatory, V4 decides those and the prototype decides how it reads; marked Unchanged, restated because point 2 could otherwise be read too widely

Decided point 5: conflict c-334 is settled by following V4's list — a cattle panel (0102) asks for a tattoo after the ear tag and the passport, a pig panel (0103) asks for a tattoo as well as an ear tag, and req-2154 and req-2155 are adopted

Decided point 5, first sub-bullet (V4 against DR1): the real frontend's commit b1ff013c deliberately removed the tattoo from cattle under DR1 parity and document:dr1-parity-notes calls asking a cow for a tattoo a defect; point 1 settles it because V4 lists Bovine in its tattoo commodity list, so the tattoo is asked for and b1ff013c's removal is reversed; it is not a silent revert, it is this ruling

Decided point 5, second sub-bullet (V4 against itself): the "Tattoo identifier commodities" expand holds five entries while its title counts two, and the entries win; not a new judgement, because sources.json already instructs the intake to "claim the entries listed, never the count", the same page titling the passport list six and listing nine; a title's count is a stale hand-written number and the list beside it is the specification; the same page naming 0102 "Bovine" in this list and "Cattle" in the others is a label difference, not a difference of scope

Decided point 6: where V4 and a DR1 judgement disagree on a shape and not just a value, V4 still wins but the shape is designed in the real service's conventions; the live example is the CPH allow-list — V4 gives fourteen chapter-01 codes that require a CPH number while main inverts it as CPH_EXEMPT_CODES under DR1 parity (fb0255c1), so every code MDM adds defaults to "CPH required", including rabbits, reptiles, parrots, bees and insects which V4 does not list; V4's allow-list wins and the deny-list goes; how the allow-list is held in code is the animals frontend's call, not V4's; marked New
What this changes in the backlog, bullet 1: req-2154 and req-2155 move from question to adopted, and c-334 stops being an open question

What this changes in the backlog, bullet 2: the tattoo coverage for cattle and pigs becomes a row in identification-and-permanent-address, the theme that owns services/commodities/rules.js and the identification page

What this changes in the backlog, bullet 3: the CPH allow-list item in deferred.md no longer waits on a V4-versus-DR1 decision, but still needs a home because it is not this theme's code — record the home it still needs as a gap claim
What this changes in the backlog, bullet 4: nothing else changes, and the ruling adds no requirement that was not already extracted; it answers questions that were
Every gap the ruling leaves open on what it touches, recorded as a gap claim rather than a decision, with no decision read from either block quote beyond what its words support
